sources.entry: Nginx Proxy Manager - Docker container for managing Nginx proxy hosts with a simple, powerful interface. (Source Code) MIT Docker
Nginx Proxy Manager | Manage Nginx proxy hosts with a simple UI and free Let's Encrypt SSL

summary.one_liner: Nginx Proxy Manager is a Docker-packaged web app for setting up Nginx reverse proxy hosts with free Let's Encrypt SSL through a simple admin interface.
summary.what_it_does: The project ships as a pre-built Docker image that forwards domain names to web services running on a home or other network, with SSL termination. The README says it lets users create forwarding domains, redirections, streams, and 404 hosts without writing Nginx configuration. It supports free Let's Encrypt certificates or custom SSL certificates. Access lists and basic HTTP authentication can be applied to hosts. Advanced Nginx configuration is available for power users, and the admin UI includes user management, permissions, and an audit log. The admin interface runs on port 81, while proxying uses ports 80 and 443.
use_cases: free SSL certificates for self-hosted websites
forward domain names to local web apps
manage Nginx proxy hosts without config files
port forwarding gateway for home network
set up HTTP redirections and streams
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml using the image docker.io/jc21/nginx-proxy-manager:latest, mapping ports 80, 81, and 443 and volumes ./data and ./letsencrypt
Open the admin UI on port 81 and log in
notable: Point-and-click proxy host setup aimed at users who know little about Nginx
Free Let's Encrypt SSL or custom certificates
Access lists and basic HTTP authentication per host
Admin UI built on Tabler with user management, permissions, and audit log
caveats: armv7 is not supported in version 2.14 and later because Node.js dropped armhf; use image tag 2.13.7 on that hardware
Home hosting requires router port forwarding for ports 80 and 443 and a domain pointed at your network
Admin UI may take a little while to come up on first start because of key generation
keywords: make my home server accessible from internet
